subject: Mutual action plan + long-context perf eval for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbushealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: MAP and perf targets for long-context pilot

Hi Ava and Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Nimbus is excited to validate Redwood for our long-document summarization pipeline. Procurement is asking for a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes specific performance acceptance criteria so we can close a pilot purchase quickly.

Key asks from Nimbus:
- Target TTFT and p95/p99 latency for 8k and 16k context lengths (generation to first token + steady-state generation).
- Throughput (tokens/sec) at concurrency points: 1, 8, 16, 32.
- Concurrency behavior for mixed prompt-size distributions (short QAs + long records).
- Impact of KV cache warm vs cold on repeated-prefix workflows.
- Timeline: pilot start, success criteria, and target close date (we'd like a vendor commitment by 2027-05-21).

Can you provide a MAP with an evaluation plan and kickoff dates? Procurement (procure@nimbushealth.com) is looped on next threads.

Best,
Sara
Director of Data Platforms
Nimbus Health

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: MAP and perf targets for long-context pilot

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Attaching an initial MAP + evaluation plan (redwood-longcontext-eval-plan.pdf) with day-by-day test cases. High-level summary below and proposed timeline so Nimbus can review with procurement: 

Proposed MAP highlights (short):
- Pilot kickoff: 2027-05-09
- Perf window: 2027-05-09 -> 2027-05-13 (5 business days of runs + verification)
- Success criteria (one of):
  - p95 latency <= 600ms, p99 <= 900ms for median 8k prompts at concurrency 8
  - Steady-state throughput >= 40k tokens/minute for mixed workload at concurrency 16
  - TTFT (time-to-first-token) for short prompts <= 120ms
- KV cache test: warm vs cold runs with 3x repeated-prefix scenarios; expect KV warm to reduce end-to-end TTFT by ~25-40% depending on model variant.

Immediate asks from Redwood:
1) Nimbus to confirm sample prompt distribution (short/medium/long). If you can share a small CSV, we'll plug it into the harness.
2) Procurement confirmation on target close date (you mentioned 2027-05-21).

Next steps:
- Marcus will run an internal quick-pass to validate the test harness against our dedicated serving pool and share preliminary numbers by EOD 2027-05-04.
- We'll schedule a 45-min results review on 2027-05-14.

Attachments: redwood-longcontext-eval-plan.pdf (plan + testcases).

Thanks — happy to adjust targets after Nimbus sample prompts land.

— Ava
Ava Chen | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-04T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: MAP and perf targets for long-context pilot (quick-pass results)

Ava / team — ran a focused quick-pass on our dedicated pool against the "long-13b" variant using the harness. Notes + raw numbers are in kvcache-quick-run-20270504.csv (attached). High-level:

Test bed: 1x p4d-equivalent node pool, model redwood-long-13b quantized, micro-batching disabled to measure per-request SLOs. Mixed prompts: 60% short (<=256 tokens), 30% medium (1k-4k), 10% long (8k-12k).

Summary results (median across 30 runs per config):
- Cold KV cache (first request for prefix)
  - Seq 4k: TTFT median 120ms, p95 420ms, p99 680ms at concurrency=8
  - Seq 8k: TTFT median 210ms, p95 660ms, p99 980ms at concurrency=8
  - Throughput (tokens/sec): ~6200 tok/s aggregate at concurrency=8 (note: tokens/sec measured during steady-state generation)

- Warm KV cache (repeated-prefix scenario)
  - Seq 4k: TTFT median 78ms, p95 210ms, p99 300ms at concurrency=8
  - Seq 8k: TTFT median 140ms, p95 380ms, p99 560ms at concurrency=8
  - Throughput (tokens/sec): ~8500 tok/s aggregate at concurrency=8

Concurrency scaling notes (Seq 8k):
- concurrency=1: p95 160ms, tokens/sec ~1100
- concurrency=8: p95 660ms, tokens/sec ~6200
- concurrency=16: p95 1150ms, tokens/sec ~9800 (note: p99 jumps disproportionately due to resource scheduling and occasional GC spikes)
- concurrency=32: we observed >10% tail amplification and occasional queueing; recommend careful autoscaling and burst limits for >16 concurrency on this model.

Observations:
- KV cache warm-up materially reduces TTFT and p99 tail; repeated-prefix workflows (EHR ingestion where same header repeats) will see 25-40% improvements in TTFT and ~30-40% throughput gains.
- Mixed prompt distributions drive micro-batching behavior if enabled — we tested with batching off to provide conservative per-request SLOs. If you enable intelligent batching, throughput can increase but p99 will need re-baselining.

I'll add these runs into the MAP doc and run a second pass with micro-batching on 2027-05-06 as requested.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin | Principal Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbushealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@nimbushealth.com, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-06T09:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: MAP and perf targets for long-context pilot

Thanks Marcus — those numbers help. A few clarifying items from Nimbus engineering: 

- Can you run the same sequence-length matrix but split prompt distributions 80/15/5 (short/medium/long) and include a cold->warm ramp for KV cache (e.g., 0, 10, 50, 200 repeated prefixes) so we can model warm-up costs?
- Please include TTFT broken out by generation path: first-token latency vs steady-state per-token latency (we need both for latency budgeting).
- For concurrency=16, can you show breakdown of p50/p95/p99 and the number of observed queue events?

Procurement asked to confirm: target close date remains 2027-05-21 if the MAP success criteria are met. Please also include an engineering contact to toggle autoscaling during pilot.

I'll share a small CSV of sample prompts (nimbus-sample-prompts.csv) by EOD.

Sara

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@nimbushealth.com>, procure@nimbushealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-08T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Final MAP + scheduled runs (kickoff 2027-05-09)

Sara / Nimbus procurement — attaching the updated MAP and the run schedule. Key items covered:

1) Scheduled test runs (planned):
   - 2027-05-09: baseline cold-KV runs (seq 4k / 8k / 12k) at conc 1/8/16
   - 2027-05-10: warm-KV ramp (0 -> 10 -> 50 -> 200 repeated prefixes)
   - 2027-05-11: mixed workload at conc 16 with micro-batching ON/OFF comparison
   - 2027-05-12: edge-case p99 stress (concurrency 32 bursts + region failover)

2) Acceptance criteria (finalized):
   - Primary: for median 8k prompts at concurrency=8, p95 <= 700ms and p99 <= 950ms
   - Secondary: steady-state throughput >= 8.5k tok/s aggregate at conc=8 for mixed workload
   - TTFT for short prompts (<=256 tokens) must be <= 140ms median

3) Roles / owners in MAP:
   - Redwood test harness & runs: Marcus Lin (marcus_lin@redwood.ai)
   - Integration/config toggles during pilot: Laura Bennett (laura_bennett@redwood.ai)
   - Commercial/contract lead: Neha Kapoor (neha_kapoor@redwood.ai)
   - Nimbus engagement / sample prompts: Sara Patel

4) Target close: 2027-05-21 assuming acceptance criteria and a short commercial redline. If the criteria are narrowly missed (<10% over p99 target), Redwood will propose a 30-day remediation SLA as a post-close term.

Attachments: redwood-longcontext-eval-plan.pdf, nimbus-sample-prompts.csv (received).

Proposed review: 2027-05-14 at 11:00 PT for go/no-go. I'll put a calendar invite after you confirm.

— Ava
Ava Chen | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
